source: the explain inventory: what users of this build need explained, refreshed for the docs (#665). An item that no longer applies has `removed` with the reason.

areas.name: First run, welcome screen and app versions

items.title: The welcome screen is the project picker
items.what: On launch Ethereal shows the "open project" dialog as a welcome screen: the logo and version, "join a jam…", "import from another daw…", "new project", a "get started" list of guides and your recent projects. Nothing opens by itself unless you turn on "reopen last project on launch".

items.title: Closing the welcome screen drops you into a draft project
items.what: Dismissing the welcome screen (Escape, ×, a click outside) with nothing open puts you in a new project named after today's date. It starts from your default project template, or the starter project (one MIDI track "Synth" with the built-in Synth).

items.title: Untouched draft projects are thrown away
items.what: A new project (from the menu, or the one you land in at launch) is kept only after you change something, undo a step or rename it. If you leave it untouched, by opening another project or quitting, it is deleted and never shows up in recent projects.

items.title: get started: guided tours and "soon" items
items.what: The welcome screen's "get started" list starts a guided tour of the real UI. Starting one makes a project for it, and finishing or leaving it brings you back to the welcome screen. Done tours show a check mark and ask "do it again?". On the mobile shell the guides are greyed out with "soon".

items.title: Reopen last project on launch (off by default)
items.what: In settings › general › startup, "reopen last project on launch" reopens your last project, but only if Ethereal closed properly last time. After a crash you choose from the recovery dialog. With it off, no plugin loads until you pick a project.

items.title: Safe mode: open without plugins
items.what: "open without plugins" (a recent project's menu, or the crash dialog) opens the project with every plugin bypassed and its state kept. The top bar then says "plugins disabled (safe mode)" and has "load plugins". The saved project isn't changed.

items.title: Only one browser tab can use Ethereal
items.what: On the web, only one tab at a time owns your projects. A second tab shows "ethereal is open in another tab" with "use here". That makes the first tab save, stop and show "ethereal moved to another tab". If the first tab doesn't answer within 8 s, the second tab takes over anyway.

items.title: Project links in the address bar (web)
items.what: The open project's address is /p/<name>/<id>. Reloading reopens it, and back / forward switch between the projects you opened. The link only works in the browser that holds the project. Anywhere else the picker says "this project isn't saved in this browser".

items.title: The "open on desktop" band
items.what: On a computer, the web version shows a band saying "Ethereal works best in the desktop app", with "open on desktop". If the app doesn't open, it offers "download Ethereal". The × hides the band only until the page reloads.

items.title: What the web version can't do
items.what: In the browser there is no plugin hosting (CLAP, VST3, AU), no recording, no MIDI learn, no hardware routing or latency measurement, no choice of audio device (the system picks), and it can't run a shared engine for others. Each place says "… needs the desktop app".

items.title: Phones and touch-only tablets are blocked
items.what: On a phone or a tablet with no mouse or trackpad, the web app shows "open this link on a computer" with "copy link" and "try the mobile beta". A tablet with a keyboard and trackpad works. Adding ?force-desktop to the address skips the check for that tab.

items.title: Project templates and the default template
items.what: Project menu › "save as template…" saves the whole project, samples included, as a template. "New project from template…" (command palette only) lets you pick a template, or "empty project", and set one as the default. Every new project then starts from that default.

items.title: Where your projects are stored
items.what: The desktop app keeps projects as folders in ~/Documents/Ethereal/Projects. The web version keeps them in this browser's private storage (OPFS), for this site only. The two are separate: a web project is not on your computer's disk, and the desktop app can't see it.

items.title: Web projects can be lost with browser data
items.what: Clearing site data or cookies for ethereal.ws, using a private window, or the browser freeing up space deletes your web projects. Ethereal doesn't ask the browser to keep its storage. Export important projects (project menu › "export project…") as backups.

items.title: Moving a project between web and desktop, or to another computer
items.what: Use project menu › "export project…" to get a .ether file, then "import project…", or drop the .ether file on the window, on the other side. The import is added as a new project, with a number if the name is taken ("Song 2").

items.title: Export project: pack media files or not
items.what: The "export project" dialog has "pack media files", on by default. On, it makes one self-contained .ether file with every audio file, including samples from your library or disk. Off, it saves the project only, and its samples show as missing on another computer.

items.title: Autosave and the unsaved-changes dot
items.what: There's no save step to remember. The project saves itself 1 s after your last edit, and the dot next to its name shows changes not saved yet. Ctrl/Cmd+S saves at once, also from text fields.

items.title: Plugin tweaks don't show the unsaved dot
items.what: Changing a plugin's own settings in its window doesn't mark the project as changed. The engine saves plugin states in the background, more slowly. Ctrl/Cmd+S reads every plugin's current state right away, and quitting the desktop app saves them too.

items.title: Closing a web tab doesn't warn you
items.what: The browser shows no "leave page?" warning. Changes save about a second after you stop editing, so wait for the dot by the project name to go before closing the tab.

items.title: Quitting the desktop app
items.what: Cmd+Q or the window's close button asks "quit Ethereal?" and says your changes are saved before it closes. Enter confirms. Live plugin states are saved too, waiting up to 30 s. If saving still fails, a copy goes to the app's "recovered" folder and the next launch tells you where.

items.title: Cmd+W closes the top floating window, not the app
items.what: In the desktop app, Cmd/Ctrl+W closes the topmost floating window, such as a device or plugin window, and doesn't quit.

items.title: The project menu
items.what: The ☰ button at the top left lists: new project, open project…, join a jam…, save as template…, the project's scale, import project…, import from another daw ▸, export project…, export to another daw ▸, export audio…, versions…, save snapshot…, delete project…, news… and (desktop) check for updates…. A click on the project's name renames it.

items.title: Some project actions are only in the command palette
items.what: "Save as…" (a copy with its media, which you then switch to), "duplicate project", "new project from template…", "relink missing samples…" and "collect all and save" are only in the command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K). Duplicate and rename are also in a recent project's ⋯ menu.

items.title: Recent projects: search, right-click menu
items.what: In "open project", type to filter recent projects and press Enter to open the first match. Right-click a project, or use its ⋯ button, for open, open without plugins, rename, duplicate, export…, sharing actions and delete…. The open project isn't listed.

items.title: Deleting a project is permanent
items.what: "Delete project…" (project menu, or a recent project's menu) asks once, then removes the project folder with all its versions. There is no trash. Deleting the open project first switches you to your most recent other project, or a new draft.

items.title: Versions: automatic backups
items.what: While you work, a version of the project is kept every minute. They are thinned to 30 spread from the last few minutes back to the first one, and named versions are never removed. Project menu › "versions…" lists them with "compare with current", "restore", rename and delete.

items.title: Restoring a version is itself reversible
items.what: "Restore" first keeps the current state as a "before restore" version, so you can go back by restoring that. Only the 10 newest unnamed "before restore" versions are kept.

items.title: Versions don't include audio files
items.what: A version only stores the project document. Media files, sharing info and exports in the project folder are never copied or restored, so a deleted or replaced sample won't come back.

items.title: Save snapshot (Mod+Alt+S)
items.what: "Save snapshot…" (project menu, command palette, or Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+S) saves a named version, such as "before the mixdown", that is kept until you delete it.

items.title: Crash recovery dialog
items.what: After Ethereal didn't close properly, launch shows "recover unsaved work?" with "recover" (opens the newer unsaved work, then save to keep it), "keep saved" and "open without plugins". If there was no unsaved work it shows "open" or "dismiss" instead. "Decide later" asks again next launch.

items.title: Missing samples and relinking
items.what: When a project's audio files can't be found, a notice says "N samples are missing" with "relink…", and those clips play silence. The relink dialog can pick a file, "search library", "search in folder…" (desktop), or "collect all and save", which copies every outside sample into the project folder. A missing clip's menu also has "relink sample…".

items.title: Samples used from your disk aren't inside the project
items.what: A sample dragged in from your library or disk stays where it is and is only referenced. Moving or deleting the original makes it missing. "Collect all and save" copies these into the project folder, as one undo step.

items.title: Files from newer or pre-release versions are refused
items.what: A project made with a newer Ethereal won't open: "this file was made with a newer version of Ethereal … Update Ethereal to open it". Projects saved by pre-release builds are no longer supported at all.

items.title: play / stop buttons and what stop does twice
items.what: the play button toggles play and pause. the square stop button stops; pressed again while stopped it returns the playhead to the selection cursor, and a third press goes to the project start.

items.title: space returns to where you started; shift+space stops in place
items.what: space plays, and pressed again it stops and jumps back to the selection (insert marker or time selection start), or to where playback started. shift+space stops and leaves the playhead where it is.

items.title: space works everywhere except text fields
items.what: space plays / stops even when a button, checkbox, menu, slider or plugin window has focus; only text boxes keep the space key. it never 'presses' the focused button.

items.title: record, loop and metronome have no default shortcut
items.what: in the default ethereal key preset, record, loop and metronome have no key. the ableton-like preset adds f9 (record) and mod+l (loop); any of them can be bound in keyboard shortcuts.

items.title: tempo field: type, drag, arrows, shift for fine
items.what: the bpm field accepts a typed value, a vertical drag (whole bpm; shift: 0.01 bpm steps) or up / down arrows (1 bpm; shift: 0.1). a whole drag is one undo step. range is 20 to 999 bpm.

items.title: the tempo field edits the tempo at the playhead, not the whole song
items.what: when the song has tempo changes, typing a bpm changes the tempo point in effect at the playhead position, not the song's first tempo.

items.title: tap tempo
items.what: click tap at least twice in rhythm to set the tempo from the average interval; a pause of more than 2 seconds starts a new count. the taps are one undo step.

items.title: time signature field is per position
items.what: the signature field shows and edits the signature at the playhead (type e.g. 7/8). to change meter mid-song, add a time signature change on the ruler instead.

items.title: position display before zero (count-in)
items.what: the position shows bars.beats.sixteenths and minutes:seconds; during a count-in it counts negative bars (e.g. -1.1.1).

items.title: metronome settings and count-in click
items.what: the metronome button toggles the click; a separate settings popover in the top bar sets volume, accent and sound (classic, wood, beep). the click also plays during a recording count-in even with the metronome off.

items.title: count-in and punch in/out
items.what: the recording controls offer a count-in of 0, 1, 2 or 4 bars, and punch in/out, which records only inside the loop region.

items.title: loop brace: move, resize, toggle, draw a new one
items.what: drag the loop brace to move it, drag its edges to resize, double-click it to turn the loop on / off; shift-drag on the ruler draws a new loop region. all snap to the grid (alt: free).

items.title: ruler: click to locate and scrub
items.what: pressing the ruler moves the playhead there and dragging scrubs it (snapped; alt: free). clicking the lanes instead places the insert marker and never moves a playing playhead.

items.title: follow playhead is off by default
items.what: the crosshair button in the arrangement's corner toolbar makes the view follow the playhead while playing: it scrolls smoothly once the playhead passes 40 % of the view width. it is off by default; on touch, panning turns it off.

items.title: tempo and time signature changes on the ruler / marker lane
items.what: right-click the ruler to add a tempo change or a time signature change there. the chips appear in the marker lane above the arrangement: drag to move (snapped; alt: free), right-click to switch ramp / hold or pick a common signature, or delete. the points at bar 1 can't move or be deleted.

items.title: tempo automation lane on the master track
items.what: the master track's 'tempo' lane shows the tempo curve: double-click the lane to add a point, double-click a point to remove it, drag to change time and bpm (shift: 0.01 bpm steps; alt: no snap), right-click for ramp to next point, delete / backspace removes the selected point.

items.title: a time signature change mid-bar cuts that bar short
items.what: a signature change can sit on any beat; placed inside a bar, that bar ends early and bar 1 of the new signature starts there.

items.title: project scale is a visual guide only
items.what: the project's scale (root and type) is set in the projects menu and is the default for every midi track's piano roll. it only highlights notes; it doesn't restrict or correct what you play.

items.title: cpu, disk and engine indicators
items.what: the right of the transport bar shows engine dsp load (cpu), a 'disk n' warning only after streamed audio dropped out (click to reset), and an engine status dot with details on hover.

items.title: adding tracks: menu, drag, or empty-space right-click
items.what: add track (corner toolbar or the row under the last track) offers midi or audio; clicking adds at the end, dragging an entry drops it between tracks or into a group. right-clicking the empty space below the tracks also adds tracks or imports audio.

items.title: new midi track opens the instrument picker
items.what: after adding a midi track, an instrument library opens under its header; picking one replaces the default synth.

items.title: track types
items.what: audio and midi tracks hold clips; group tracks hold other tracks (cmd/ctrl+g); vca tracks control other tracks' volume; return tracks and the pinned master sit at the bottom. groups can hold audio, midi and groups, not returns or vcas.

items.title: selecting tracks: click, shift, cmd/ctrl
items.what: click a header to select a track (the inspector shows it); shift-click selects a range; cmd/ctrl-click toggles. clicking empty lane space also selects that track.

items.title: solo is exclusive; cmd/ctrl-click adds
items.what: a plain click on solo solos only that track (clicking the only soloed track unsolos it); cmd/ctrl-click adds or removes it from the soloed set.

items.title: arm is exclusive; cmd/ctrl-click to arm several
items.what: clicking arm arms only that track; cmd/ctrl-click arms more. arming an audio track with no input device open asks you to choose one.

items.title: header volume and pan
items.what: each header has a small horizontal volume fader (drag; shift: fine; double-click: 0 db; the db shows on hover) and a pan knob (drag up / down; double-click: center). with several tracks selected, dragging one fader moves all of them by the same db, keeping their balance.

items.title: rename tracks; empty name restores the default
items.what: double-click a track name to rename (enter / click away saves, escape cancels). clearing the name goes back to its default; an unnamed midi track shows its instrument's name.

items.title: reorder tracks by dragging headers
items.what: drag a header vertically to move the track; drop between rows to place it there, or over the middle of a group's header to put it inside the group. groups move with their children; returns reorder among the returns only (the regular tracks show as a not-allowed zone) and master stays at the bottom. edge auto-scroll, escape cancels, one undo step per move.

items.title: track height, header width
items.what: drag a header's bottom edge to resize the track in steps (alt: free); double-click resets it. the edge between the headers and the lanes resizes the header column (double-click resets); a narrow column moves the grid picker into a 'more' menu.

items.title: zoom and scroll with wheel, trackpad, middle button
items.what: by default the wheel scrolls; cmd/ctrl+wheel zooms time; cmd/ctrl+shift+wheel zooms all track heights; shift+wheel scrolls sideways; a trackpad pinch always zooms; middle-button drag pans. all of this is configurable in settings > input (zoom modifier, plain-wheel zoom, inversion, sensitivity); windows inverts zoom by default.

items.title: zoom out stops past the song end
items.what: zooming out stops a little past the last clip or marker (at least 32 bars of 4/4 wide), so an empty song can't zoom out further.

items.title: grid and snap; alt bypasses everywhere
items.what: the grid picker sets adaptive (narrow / medium / wide), 1 bar, 1/4, 1/8, 1/16 or off. every arrangement drag snaps to it: clips, trims, slips, loop brace, markers, tempo points, time selections, take swipes. holding alt/option while dragging (or clicking) bypasses the snap.

items.title: click on a lane places the insert marker, not the playhead
items.what: a plain click on empty lane space (or a clip's body) places a blinking insert marker on that track, snapped (alt: free). paste, split and insert land there, never at the playhead. while stopped the playhead jumps to it; while playing it takes effect at the next stop.

items.title: plain drag selects clips, shift-drag selects time
items.what: dragging over the lanes draws a box that selects clips; shift-drag instead makes a time selection across tracks (you can press or release shift mid-drag to switch). a click clears it.

items.title: plain edit keys act on the time selection when one exists
items.what: with a time selection, cmd/ctrl+c / x / v / d and delete act on the section (clips cut at its edges), not on whole clips. without one, they act on selected clips. the last copy wins cmd/ctrl+v (clips, tracks or time).

items.title: time edits: insert silence, delete time, duplicate, paste
items.what: shortcuts on a time selection: shift+cmd/ctrl+i insert silence, shift+cmd/ctrl+backspace delete time (later material moves left), cmd/ctrl+d duplicate time (over what follows), cmd/ctrl+v paste over (after the selection), shift+cmd/ctrl+v paste-insert (shifts what follows). right-click inside the selection for the same menu plus bounce to new track.

items.title: selecting all tracks moves markers and tempo too
items.what: a time edit on a selection that covers every track also shifts markers, tempo points and time signatures; on fewer tracks only clips, takes and automation move.

items.title: paste overwrites; time clipboard is not saved
items.what: paste and duplicate of a time section go over what is already there (use paste-insert to push material right). the time clipboard lives in the engine and is lost when the app restarts.

items.title: undo restores selections
items.what: undo and redo bring back the time selection, the selected clips and notes as they were for that step.

items.title: markers (locators)
items.what: the marker lane above the arrangement: double-click empty space or press + to add (at the cursor; while playing, at the playhead). click a marker to jump, drag to move (alt: free), double-click to rename, right-click for jump / rename / delete.

items.title: group and ungroup tracks
items.what: cmd/ctrl+g groups the selected tracks (tracks from different groups move together first); cmd/ctrl+shift+g ungroups. click a group's round badge to fold or unfold it; a folded group's lane shows a summary of its clips. ungrouping a group with devices, automation, sends or routings asks first because those are lost.

items.title: vca tracks
items.what: right-click selected tracks > new vca for track(s) creates a vca that controls their volume; assign or remove others from the same menu or the inspector's vca row.

items.title: track menu: cut, copy, paste, duplicate, delete tracks
items.what: right-click a header (or use cmd/ctrl+c / x / v / d and delete) to act on all selected tracks; labels show the count ('delete 3 tracks'). duplicate copies devices, clips, automation and sends.

items.title: cut tracks can only be pasted right away
items.what: cutting tracks deletes them; pasting restores them only while the cut is still the latest undo step. after any other edit the cut tracks can no longer be pasted (undo still brings them back).

items.title: track input from another track
items.what: an audio track's input can be another track (resampling or bus-to-track) with a tap point (pre fx, post fx, post mixer); choosing one turns monitoring to in.

items.title: arrangement shortcuts need the arrangement focused
items.what: clip and time shortcuts (split, duplicate, delete, arrows for takes) work when the arrangement has focus; clicking in it gives focus. escape deselects (and closes the piano roll).

items.title: grab clips by their title bar
items.what: drag a clip by its title band to move it, by its left / right edge to trim. the clip's body lets clicks through to the lane (insert marker, selection box, fade handles), so dragging the body does not move it.

items.title: cmd/ctrl-drag copies (not alt)
items.what: hold cmd (mac) or ctrl while releasing a clip drag to copy instead of move; pressing or releasing it mid-drag switches at once. alt/option does not copy: it disables snapping.

items.title: clip selection modifiers
items.what: click selects a clip (and its track); shift-click adds; cmd/ctrl-click toggles; a plain click on an already selected clip narrows to just it. while stopped, pressing a clip moves the playhead to its start.

items.title: click opens the clip editor
items.what: pressing a midi clip opens it in the piano roll; clicking an audio clip (without dragging or modifiers) opens its editor drawer (warp, envelopes). clicking elsewhere closes it unless pinned.

items.title: double-click expands the editor and inspector
items.what: double-clicking a clip (or a take's clip) opens it in the editor and expands the editor drawer and the inspector if they were collapsed, at their last size; a panel already open keeps its size. With both expanded, double-clicking the clip already open collapses both (a toggle); another clip switches the editor to it and both stay open.

items.title: moving onto other clips trims or deletes them
items.what: dropping, pasting or resizing a clip over others on the same track trims clips it partly covers, deletes clips it fully covers and splits a clip it lands inside (crossfades are kept).

items.title: moving clips between tracks and to new tracks
items.what: drag a clip up or down to another track of the same kind (audio to audio, midi to midi); if any target doesn't fit, the clips stay on their tracks. drag below the last track to create new tracks for them (shown as ghost lanes), one undo step.

items.title: trimming limits and leading gaps
items.what: trimming the end of an unlooped audio clip stops at the end of its file; with loop on it repeats. trimming the start past the content start leaves silent space before it. the shortest clip is 1/16 beat.

items.title: slip edit: cmd/ctrl+shift-drag
items.what: hold ctrl+shift (cmd+shift on mac) and drag a clip's body to move its content inside the clip without moving the clip; snapped (alt: free); escape cancels. it stops at the file's ends, so a clip showing the whole file can't slip.

items.title: create midi clips with double-click
items.what: double-click an empty midi lane to make a one-bar clip; double-click and drag (keep holding on the second press) to set its length on the grid (alt: free). audio lanes take dropped files instead.

items.title: drag and drop audio
items.what: drop audio files or browser samples on an audio track's lane to create clips at the drop point (several files go one after another); drop below the tracks to get a new audio track per file. midi tracks refuse audio. an 'importing… %' placeholder shows progress. alt while dropping disables snapping.

items.title: split, duplicate, loop, reverse shortcuts
items.what: cmd/ctrl+e splits at the insert marker (or the time selection edges); cmd/ctrl+d duplicates right after; cmd/ctrl+shift+l toggles clip loop; r reverses. the clip right-click menu has the same plus mute, rename and delete.

items.title: paste goes to the insert marker and tiles
items.what: pasting clips puts them at the insert marker (else where you right-clicked), keeping their spacing; the marker then moves to the end so pasting again continues the pattern. clips go back to their own tracks unless all came from one track and another track is selected.

items.title: rename clips
items.what: right-click a single clip > rename edits its name in the title bar (enter saves, escape cancels). an empty name restores the default (an audio clip's sample name). with several clips selected rename is not offered.

items.title: clip and track colors
items.what: colors are set in the inspector: clip color (for all selected clips) or 'use the track color', and track color. new tracks get a palette color.

items.title: fade handles on audio clips
items.what: hover or select an audio clip to see fade handles at its top corners: drag sideways to set fade length, drag the midpoint handle up / down to bend the curve (double-click: linear). right-click switches all selected clips between linear and equal-power fades. fades are also typed in the inspector.

items.title: crossfades between touching clips
items.what: drag a fade handle past the clip edge into a touching or overlapping neighbor to create a crossfade; drag it back to almost nothing to remove it. right-click also offers crossfade with previous / next clip (default half a beat) and remove crossfade.

items.title: clip gain changes the waveform height
items.what: an audio clip's gain (inspector) scales its waveform; parts that would pass full scale are flattened and marked in the clip color.

items.title: editing several clips in the inspector
items.what: with several audio clips selected, typing a gain, transpose or warp value sets it on all; dragging or stepping moves all by the same amount, keeping their differences. mixed values show as mixed.

items.title: reverse
items.what: r (or right-click > reverse) reverses audio clips (a 'rev' badge shows; pressing again unreverses) and mirrors midi clips' notes and controllers in time. a trimmed audio clip plays the same part of the file backwards; fades stay at the clip edges.

items.title: warp: on/off, repitch or complex
items.what: the audio clip editor's warp tab toggles warp and picks repitch (speed and pitch follow the tempo) or complex (keeps pitch). it shows the detected source tempo or 'source tempo unknown'. where no time-stretch engine exists, complex plays as repitch and the editor says so.

items.title: warp markers
items.what: with warp on, double-click the waveform to add a marker; drag it to re-time the audio (snapped to 1/16; alt: free); double-click a marker or select it and press delete to remove it. a marker only stretches the audio between its neighbors; the first marker also pins the file's start and end.

items.title: takes: where they come from
items.what: recording several loop passes, punching in, or recording over existing clips turns each pass into a take lane (the newest plays). a track with takes shows a takes button in its header (with the count) to show or hide the lanes; right-click the header > new take lane adds one by hand.

items.title: swipe comping and choosing takes
items.what: drag across a take lane to make that range play from this take (snapped; alt: free); a click picks the take for the region under the pointer. then up / down arrows step through takes for the selected region. audition (headphones) plays one take alone.

items.title: take lane menu: crossfades, promote, flatten
items.what: right-click a take lane: audition, comp whole take, promote clip to main lane, remove from comp, region crossfade (none, 5, 20, 100 ms), rename, move up / down, delete take. flatten comp bakes the comp; 'flatten comp and delete takes' discards the other takes, after a confirmation (#717).

items.title: freeze locks clips and devices
items.what: right-click a track (or group) > freeze renders it to save cpu; while frozen (snowflake in the header) its clips, devices and device automation can't be edited, but volume, pan, mute, solo and sends still work. click the snowflake to unfreeze. renders run one at a time and show progress (click to cancel).

items.title: freezing a group locks its tracks
items.what: a frozen group plays one render; tracks inside show a lock and can't be edited, moved, soloed or muted until the group is unfrozen. their sends to returns stop.

items.title: flatten is permanent
items.what: flatten replaces a frozen track's clips and devices with one audio clip of the render (a midi track becomes an audio track; a group becomes one audio track). it asks first (#717); only undo brings them back.

items.title: bounce to new track, bounce in place, consolidate
items.what: clip menu: bounce to new track renders the selected clips' span with effects and their tail (up to 30 s) to a new audio track below and mutes the source; bounce in place (audio only) renders without effects, replacing the clips; consolidate joins selected clips into one per track. a time selection's menu also has bounce to new track.

items.title: Draw a note: double-click empty space (or turn on draw mode)
items.what: A single click on empty grid only places the insert marker. A double-click adds a note, and keeping the button down after the second press and dragging sets its length. The draw button (shortcut B) makes every press draw.

items.title: New notes are one grid step long
items.what: A drawn note takes the current grid step as its length (the step shown next to the grid select), not the length of the last note you drew. Change the grid, or drag while drawing, to get longer notes.

items.title: Delete a note by double-clicking it
items.what: A double-click on a note deletes it, but only when both clicks land on that same note. Delete/Backspace and the right-click menu's "delete note" also work.

items.title: Move, resize and transpose by dragging
items.what: Drag a note's body to move it in time and pitch. Drag either edge to resize it. When several notes are selected they all move together, and their pitch intervals are kept.

items.title: Pressing a note plays it (the headphones toggle)
items.what: Pressing a note or a key in the keyboard gutter plays it on the track's instrument while you hold it. A vertical drag plays the note again at its new pitch. The headphones button turns this off, and that choice is remembered.

items.title: Selecting notes: click, Shift, Cmd/Ctrl, marquee, select all
items.what: Click selects a note. Shift-click adds to the selection and Cmd/Ctrl-click toggles a note (applied on release). Dragging on empty space draws a marquee. Cmd/Ctrl+A selects every shown note and Esc clears the selection.

items.title: Click a piano key to select all notes of that pitch
items.what: Clicking a key in the keyboard gutter plays the pitch and selects every note on that row. Shift and Cmd/Ctrl add to the selection the same way they do on notes.

items.title: Alt/Option-drag a note to change its velocity
items.what: Holding Alt/Option over a note changes the cursor to up/down. A vertical drag then changes the velocity of the pressed note, or of the whole selection by the same amount, and a badge shows the value. Adding Shift gives fine control.

items.title: Cmd/Ctrl-drag duplicates notes, and you can switch mid-drag
items.what: Holding Cmd/Ctrl while dragging a note (pressed at the start or during the drag) leaves the originals in place and drags copies. Releasing Cmd/Ctrl during the drag removes the copies and moves the originals again. The cursor shows "copy".

items.title: Turning snapping off: Shift when moving, Alt for everything else
items.what: When moving notes, Shift (or Alt pressed during the drag) turns off grid snapping. When drawing, resizing, marquee/section selecting, clicking to place the marker, dragging the stretch bar or dragging expression points, Alt/Option does. Alt pressed at the start of a move edits velocity instead.

items.title: Shift-drag on empty space makes a time section
items.what: A plain drag on empty grid selects notes. A Shift-drag also makes a section (a time range across those rows) and selects the notes under it, and you can press or release Shift during the drag to switch. Dragging on the strip under the ruler selects a section too.

items.title: With a section, copy/cut/paste/duplicate use its exact length
items.what: When a section is selected, Cmd/Ctrl+C, X, V and D work on the section's time span, gaps included, and notes are cut at its edges. Delete clears what is inside the section. Without a section they act on the selected notes.

items.title: Arrow keys nudge notes (Shift: octave)
items.what: Up/Down move the selected notes one semitone and Shift+Up/Down one octave. Left/Right move them one grid step (with or without Shift). All of these can be changed in the keymap.

items.title: Click empty grid to set where playback starts
items.what: A click on empty space places the insert marker, snapped to the grid (Alt: free). While stopped, play starts from there. It never moves the playhead while playing.

items.title: Velocity lane
items.what: The lane under the grid shows velocity as bars by default. Dragging a bar up or down changes it, or changes the whole selection if that bar is selected. Hovering a bar shows its value.

items.title: Quantize: Cmd/Ctrl+U uses the quantize… popover settings
items.what: The quantize button and Cmd/Ctrl+U apply the settings from the "quantize…" popover: grid (default "roll grid"), strength, swing and "quantize ends". They act on the selected notes, or on every note in the clip when nothing is selected.

items.title: Quantize and humanize settings are remembered
items.what: The values you set in the quantize… and humanize… popovers are kept on this computer (app-wide, not per project) and survive a restart (#717).

items.title: Humanize randomizes timing and velocity
items.what: The humanize… popover (also in the note right-click menu) shifts timing randomly by up to ±1/16 at 100% and varies velocity. It works on the selection or the whole clip, and each run gives a new random result.

items.title: Project swing vs quantize swing
items.what: The project swing ("groove" row of the clip inspector, 1/8 or 1/16 grid) delays off-beats of every MIDI clip during playback without moving any notes. The swing inside quantize… writes the swing into the notes of one clip.

items.title: Scales are a visual guide only
items.what: The scale… popover sets the track scale (follow project scale, custom track scale, chromatic / none), with highlight and "scale notes only". Nothing is quantized to the scale: MIDI input, recording and arrow-key nudges can still produce any pitch.

items.title: "Scale notes only" hides notes that are still there
items.what: With "scale notes only" on, out-of-scale rows are folded away, but their notes still play and are kept. Select all only takes the shown notes. Turn the toggle off to see or draw other pitches.

items.title: Editing the scale in follow-project mode changes every track
items.what: When the track follows the project scale, changing the root or type in the scale… popover edits the project scale, so it applies to every track that follows it. Switch to custom track scale to change only this track.

items.title: Stretch bar, ×2 / ÷2 and reverse
items.what: A bar on the ruler spans the selection: drag its edges to time-stretch the notes (Alt: no snap), or drag its body to move them. ×2 and ÷2 double or halve the length from the start. Reverse mirrors the selected notes, or the section, in time.

items.title: Key height grip and triplet grid
items.what: Drag the grip above the keyboard up or down to resize the keys, and double-click it to reset. The "3" button switches the grid to triplets.

items.title: Edit several MIDI clips at once
items.what: Select several MIDI clips in the arrangement and open one (or use the clip menu's "edit N clips in piano roll") to edit all of them on the song timeline. Notes of the unfocused clips are dimmed, and clicking a clip's band or one of its notes focuses that clip.

items.title: Multi-clip: notes can't leave their clip, and clips never grow
items.what: When editing several clips, a moved note is clamped to its own clip's region. Nothing is drawn outside a clip, and a paste drops any notes that land over no clip.

items.title: Looping clips: only the first pass is real
items.what: In a looping clip, the repeats after the loop are ghosts of the loop's notes. Drawing in a repeat writes the note into the loop itself, so it appears in every pass.

items.title: Drum Rack tracks open the beat editor
items.what: On a Drum Rack track the editor is a step grid: one row per pad. Left click toggles a hit, right click removes one, and dragging along a row paints or erases. The "beat editor | piano roll" tabs at the right of the toolbar switch editors.

items.title: Expression lanes: CC, pitch bend, pressure
items.what: The lane picker under the grid switches between velocity, per-note pressure/pitch/timbre, clip expression (pitch bend, channel pressure, CC 1, 11, 64, "other CC…" for any 0–119) and the clip's device envelopes. A "•" marks lanes that already contain data.

items.title: Drawing and editing expression curves
items.what: In a clip lane, dragging on the background draws a curve with a pencil. Dragging a point moves it, snapped to the grid (Alt: free). Double-clicking adds or deletes a point. Right-click offers clear and remove lane, and the "remove lane" button deletes it; clearing, or removing a lane with points, asks first (#717).

items.title: Per-note lanes draw over the selected notes only
items.what: In a per-note lane (pressure, pitch, timbre), a pencil stroke only writes to the selected notes, or to all shown notes when none is selected. Right-click › clear clears those notes' curves, after a confirmation (#717). Curve points after a note's end are kept but not played.

items.title: MPE: turn it on per track in the inspector
items.what: A MIDI track's inspector has MPE settings: enabled, zone (lower: master 1 / upper: master 16), member channels, and the note and master bend ranges. With MPE on, recorded per-note pitch/pressure/timbre become per-note curves, and pitch curves are drawn inside the notes.

items.title: Convert audio to MIDI
items.what: Right-click an audio clip and choose "convert to MIDI…". Pick melody, harmony or drums, set the sensitivity and range (or the drum keys), and optionally add a Poly Synth or a Drum Rack with a kit. The result goes on a new MIDI track right below the source track.

items.title: Audio to MIDI: one conversion at a time, main-lane clips only
items.what: Only one conversion runs at a time, and the menu entry is disabled while another one runs. "Hide" keeps it running with a progress bar on the clip (click it to stop). Only clips on the main lane can be converted, not take lanes.

items.title: Computer MIDI keyboard (M)
items.what: Press M or click the piano button in the transport bar. The home row A–; then plays notes (W E T Y U O P are the black keys), Z/X shift the octave and C/V change the velocity in steps of 20. It plays like a hardware MIDI input: monitored tracks hear it and armed tracks record it.

items.title: While the MIDI keyboard is on, letter shortcuts stop working
items.what: With the computer keyboard on, its note and control keys (A–;, W–P, Z X C V) play notes instead of running shortcuts, for example B for draw mode. Shortcuts with Cmd/Ctrl/Alt and Space still work. It also stays on after a restart.

items.title: The MIDI keyboard auto-arms a track
items.what: If no MIDI track would hear the computer keyboard, turning it on (or playing) arms the selected MIDI track, as Ableton does. The tooltip names the track it plays on, or says to add a MIDI track.

items.title: The MIDI keyboard keeps playing inside plugin windows
items.what: On desktop, native plugin editor windows forward their keystrokes, so the computer keyboard keeps playing while a plugin's window has focus.

items.title: Piano roll on touch: select and draw modes
items.what: In the mobile UI, double-tap a clip to open the editor. In select mode, tap selects and dragging empty space pans. In draw mode, tap adds a note. Double-tap adds or deletes a note, long-press opens a note's menu, and long-press then drag makes a selection box. Pinch zooms time (fingers side by side) or key height (one above the other).

items.title: Recording needs the desktop app
items.what: In the browser the record and punch buttons are disabled, and the inputs panel says "recording needs the desktop app". The browser has no audio or MIDI hardware inputs. The computer MIDI keyboard and capture still work there.

items.title: Arm a track, then record
items.what: Click ● on a track header to arm it, then press the record button in the transport bar. Stopping turns everything recorded into clips as one undo step. Record has no default shortcut (the Ableton keymap preset uses F9).

items.title: Arming is exclusive; Cmd/Ctrl-click arms several
items.what: A plain click on a track's ● arms that track and disarms the others. Ctrl/Cmd-click adds it to the armed set. The arm buttons in the IN ▾ panel never disarm other tracks.

items.title: Arm state is remembered per project on this computer
items.what: Which tracks are armed is runtime state: not in the project file and not undoable. It is kept on this computer per project and comes back when the project is reopened (#717).

items.title: Arming an audio track with no input device opens settings
items.what: If you arm an audio track and the engine has no input device open, settings open on the audio tab with "choose an input device to record from". Without an input, recordings would be silent.

items.title: The IN ▾ panel: input device, per-track arm, input and monitor
items.what: The IN ▾ button next to record opens a panel with the audio input device and a table of audio/MIDI tracks: arm, input ("no input", each mono channel, stereo pairs like "1/2", or a MIDI port / "all ports") and monitor.

items.title: Monitor modes: auto, in, off
items.what: Auto (the default) monitors the input while the track is armed. In always passes the input through. Off never does. Monitoring an input through the speakers with a microphone can cause feedback.

items.title: MIDI input port and channel filters
items.what: A MIDI track's input can be "all ports" or one port, plus "all channels" or Ch 1–16. Each armed MIDI track only records the messages its filter accepts, so two controllers (or channels) can record to two tracks at once.

items.title: Count-in (pre-roll)
items.what: The count-in select (off, 1, 2 or 4 bars, saved with the project) starts playback that many bars before the record position. Nothing played during the count-in is kept.

items.title: Punch records only inside the loop region
items.what: With PUNCH on, only what is played inside the loop region is kept, and every pass becomes a take. The punch range is the loop brace; there are no separate punch markers. The toggle is kept on this computer per project, like the arms (#717).

items.title: Recording over clips or in a loop makes takes, not overdub
items.what: Recording over existing clips, recording several loop passes or punching in turns each pass into a take lane, with the newest selected. Existing clips move onto the first take lane. MIDI is never merged into an existing clip; there is no overdub mode.

items.title: Takes: show lanes, swipe to comp, Up/Down to switch
items.what: The takes button on the track header shows the take lanes. Dragging across a lane plays that range from that take. Clicking picks the take for a region, and Up/Down then step through the takes.

items.title: Live view while recording
items.what: While recording, a growing "recording" clip shows the waveform or the notes played, and held notes grow. When you stop, it is replaced by the real clips in the same spot.

items.title: Silent take warning (macOS microphone permission)
items.what: If a take is pure digital silence for at least a second, a warning explains that macOS may have denied microphone access (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone), and to check the device and channels.

items.title: Switching projects while recording finishes the recording first
items.what: Opening or creating another project while recording stops the recording first: the takes go into the project they were recorded in, which is saved before the switch (#717).

items.title: Recording another track (resampling)
items.what: Set an audio track's input to another track to record that track's output. It is aligned with its own latency. This is desktop only: in the browser, arming such a track is disabled.

items.title: Capture MIDI: rescue what you just played
items.what: The capture button in the transport bar is always listening, even without arming or recording. Clicking it turns what you just played into a clip on the selected MIDI track, or else the first armed MIDI track, or else the first MIDI track (a new one if there is none).

items.title: Capture while stopped sets the tempo (empty projects only)
items.what: Notes played while stopped become the last phrase (after a gap of 6 seconds) and are placed at the playhead. In an empty project, capture also guesses the tempo (60–180 bpm, with the first note as the downbeat) and sets the loop to the clip. Notes played while the transport runs keep their song positions.

items.title: Capture keeps only the latest take, then empties
items.what: Every play/stop starts a new capture take, and capture uses only the latest one that has notes. After a capture the buffer is emptied. It holds up to 10 minutes and is cleared when you switch projects. It is never saved or shared in a jam.

items.title: Capture respects the target track's MIDI filter
items.what: Only messages that pass the target track's input port and channel filter are captured. If the selected track listens to another port or channel, capture says nothing was played.

items.title: Settings > audio: driver, output, input, sample rate, buffer
items.what: The gear opens settings. The audio tab has the driver (only shown when there is more than one, such as ASIO and WASAPI), output device, input device ("none (no recording)" by default), sample rate and buffer size. Every change applies immediately and is remembered for next time.

items.title: In the browser, the system picks the devices
items.what: On the web, the audio tab cannot list or change devices. It says "your system chooses the devices", so you change them in the OS or browser.

items.title: Buffer size: what you ask for vs what the device runs
items.what: The buffer select (32–2048 samples, limited to what the device supports) shows the size the device actually runs. A note appears when the device runs a different size than you asked for. With WASAPI shared mode, Windows sets it, so use an ASIO driver to choose it.

items.title: Smaller buffer = lower latency, more dropouts
items.what: The status line shows the running rate, buffer, output/input latency in ms and the dropout count. A smaller buffer lowers latency but raises the risk of dropouts (crackles).

items.title: Recording latency is compensated automatically
items.what: Recorded audio and MIDI are placed using the round-trip latency the driver reports (input + output + buffering). There is no manual latency offset setting, so a driver that misreports its latency gives takes that are slightly off.

items.title: Input check
items.what: At the bottom of the audio tab, input check shows a meter for each armed track. It needs an input device chosen, a track armed and monitoring on.

items.title: Refresh devices after plugging in
items.what: The refresh button on the audio tab lists the devices again, for example after plugging in an interface.

items.title: Unplugged output: automatic fallback and return
items.what: If the output device disappears (USB unplugged, Bluetooth off), a warning names it and the engine switches to the default output, or plays silently if that fails too. It switches back when the device returns ("is back"). Your saved settings don't change.

items.title: "Device closed" status when another engine plays
items.what: When the session plays through another engine ("play with"), the audio tab shows "device closed: no local engine plays". The device opens again with the same settings when you switch back.

items.title: Engine not responding notice
items.what: If the engine stalls (for example a plugin busy opening its editor), a warning says "the engine is not responding" with the reason when known. Audio keeps playing, and your actions run when it recovers. A summary of how long it lasted follows.

items.title: Engine log (desktop)
items.what: Settings > advanced > "open engine log" opens a terminal that follows the engine's log: warnings, plugin problems and the reason for stalls.

items.title: MIDI controllers just work (no device list)
items.what: There is no MIDI device settings page: every connected MIDI input port opens automatically. You choose ports per track in the IN ▾ panel ("all ports" by default). Hardware MIDI works only in the desktop app; the web build has none yet.

items.title: MIDI mapping: turn on MIDI mode, click a control, move a knob
items.what: Open the "MIDI mapping" tab in the left rail and turn on MIDI mode. Mappable controls light up. Click one (click again to cancel), then move a knob or press a key on your controller. Esc cancels a learn in progress.

items.title: Right-click any control: learn MIDI / remove MIDI mapping
items.what: While MIDI mode is on, right-clicking a mappable control offers "learn MIDI" and "remove MIDI mapping". For targets without a control (transport actions, or arm/mute/solo of the selected track), use "learn other target…" in the panel.

items.title: Mappings are saved in the project, not globally
items.what: MIDI mappings belong to the project file. Adding, editing and removing them can be undone, and they don't carry over to other projects. There is no global controller setup.

items.title: One mapping per knob: learning again replaces it
items.what: Each controller source (port, channel, CC/note) can drive only one target. Learning a knob that is already used moves it to the new target.

items.title: Mapping options: mode, min and max
items.what: Each mapping in the list has a mode (absolute, three relative encoder types, toggle) and min/max percentages. Setting min above max inverts the control. Right-click a mapping for "learn again" or "remove mapping", or click ✕.

items.title: Mapped keys still play notes
items.what: MIDI used by a mapping still reaches monitored tracks. A pad mapped to play/stop will also trigger a note on an armed or monitored instrument.

items.title: MIDI learn needs the desktop app
items.what: In the browser, the MIDI mode switch is disabled ("MIDI learn needs the desktop app"), because Web MIDI is not wired yet.

items.title: adding a device
items.what: each chain section (midi effects, instrument, audio effects) has its own + button or "+ add device…"; it opens the device library with search, all / factory / plugins chips, favourites (star) and sort (name, most used, most recent). a click or enter adds it and opens its window.

items.title: instruments only on midi tracks, one per chain
items.what: instruments and midi effects can only go on midi tracks; audio tracks take audio effects only. a chain has one instrument: adding another instrument from the library replaces the current one (one undo step).

items.title: chain order is fixed by section
items.what: midi effects always sit before the instrument and audio effects after it; reordering only works inside a section (drag the header, or the ‹ › buttons in the row layout).

items.title: device window vs parameter list
items.what: the device card only shows its header. the window button opens the device's own ui (factory window or plugin editor); the sliders button shows a generic, searchable parameter list on the card. the two are independent, and window positions are remembered per device on this machine.

items.title: bypass, rename, copy / paste devices
items.what: the power button bypasses a device; double-click the name to rename (empty name restores the original); click a card then ⌘c / ⌘v (ctrl on windows/linux) copies and pastes it after the selected one, including plugin state, rack chains or drum pads. right-click the header for copy, paste after, rename, bypass, group into rack, add modulator, delete.

items.title: hover-only header buttons
items.what: the preset button and the + modulator button in a device header only appear while the pointer is over the card.

items.title: knob gestures
items.what: drag a knob up/down to change it; hold shift while dragging for fine control (10x slower); double-click resets to the default; arrow keys / page up / page down / home / end work when focused (shift = finer). horizontal sliders: click the track to jump, drag the thumb, shift = fine.

items.title: touch knobs: fine mode by moving sideways
items.what: on touch, the further your finger moves sideways off the knob while dragging vertically, the finer the change.

items.title: no typing values into knobs
items.what: device knobs can't be typed into; set exact values by fine-dragging, arrow keys, or (for automation points) right-click > set value…. a few widgets (number fields, the multisampler's zone inspector) do take typed numbers.

items.title: parameter context menu
items.what: right-click any device parameter for "show automation lane" (opens that parameter's lane under the track) and "reset to default". automated parameters show a small automated marker.

items.title: show all parameters and pinning
items.what: for plugins with many parameters the card shows a capped list; "show all n parameters…" opens a searchable list where you pin parameters to the card. pins apply to every instance of that plugin in every project, and are kept on this machine only.

items.title: presets: load, save, factory vs user
items.what: the preset button in a device header lists factory presets then your own; a click loads one (one undo step). "save preset…" takes a name and tags; saving over an existing name needs a second click on replace. right-click your presets to rename or delete. plugins get presets too (their full state is saved).

items.title: presets are files in your user library
items.what: user presets are saved as .etherpreset files under presets/<device>/ in the user library (plugins under presets/plugins/<format>/<id>/), so they're shared across projects and also show in the browser's presets view. sampler presets copy their samples into the library's samples/ folder.

items.title: current preset name is per session
items.what: the preset button shows the last preset loaded in this session only; after reopening a project it no longer shows which preset a device came from, and any knob change doesn't mark it as modified.

items.title: device library favourites, sort and format toggles
items.what: star a row to favourite it, filter to favourites only, sort by name / most used / most recent. when plugins exist in several formats, clap / vst3 / au chips toggle which formats are listed (at least one stays on). all of this is remembered on this machine.

items.title: synth
items.what: simple polyphonic synth (16 voices): sine / saw / square / triangle, adsr, low-pass filter with env amount (the amp envelope sweeps the cutoff ±6 octaves) and key tracking, fine, glide, velocity sensitivity, and mode poly / mono / legato (legato glides only on overlapping notes, last-note priority). 5 factory presets.

items.title: poly synth
items.what: 2 oscillators (saw / square / triangle / sine / wavetable with 8 tables and a position morph), sub and noise, multimode filter with drive, amp / filter / mod envelopes, 2 lfos with a target and amount each, unison up to 16 voices (detune in cents, blend, spread), drift, glide, bend range, voice mode. osc 2 and sub start silent (-70 db).

items.title: fm synth
items.what: four operators a–d in one of 11 algorithms (the diagram picks it), each with wave, ratio (coarse + fine) or fixed frequency, level, adsr, velocity and self-feedback; a filter (off by default) with its own envelope, one lfo (to pitch / filter / volume), tone, antialias (2x oversampling, on). only operator a is audible by default.

items.title: sampler
items.what: plays one sample: one-shot (whole sample, note-off ignored) or pitched (follows key minus root key). start / end range, reverse, loop forward or ping-pong with crossfade (pitched mode only), filter, adsr, up to 32 voices. its window opens a sample picker on first open; drop a sample from the browser onto it.

items.title: sampler slice mode
items.what: the sampler window's classic | slice switch: slice mode cuts the sample into slices (transients with a sensitivity, beat grid or equal parts; switching on a sample without slices finds its transients). the first key plays slice 1, the next key slice 2, other keys are ignored. markers: double-click adds, drag moves, double-click / delete / right-click removes; pressing a slice plays it. "slice to drum rack" replaces the sampler by a drum rack with one pad per slice.

items.title: multisampler
items.what: zones with key and velocity ranges, root key, tune, gain, pan, loops and round-robin (cycle or random). drop several files from your computer onto a key to map them (roots read from names like c3 or 60); drag zone bodies/edges to move or resize; delete removes the selected zone.

items.title: compressor
items.what: threshold, ratio, attack, release, makeup, knee, mix (parallel), detector peak / rms / expand (expand turns it into a downward expander), lookahead up to 10 ms (adds latency), auto makeup, and sidechain hpf (only for a sidechain source). 4 factory presets.

items.title: eq
items.what: 8-band parametric eq (low cut, low shelf, bell, notch, high shelf, high cut), channel stereo / left / right / mid / side, live spectrum. on the curve: drag a handle for frequency + gain, alt-drag or wheel for q, shift = fine, double-click toggles a band, right-click for type and reset; arrow keys on a focused handle.

items.title: delay
items.what: time in ms or synced to tempo (up to 5 s), feedback, mix, ping-pong (sums to mono and bounces left/right), low / high cut inside the feedback loop (each repeat darker), mod rate / depth (tape wobble), freeze (loops what's in the line).

items.title: grain delay
items.what: echoes made of short overlapping grains: pitch (-36..+12, cascades with feedback), frequency (grain rate and size), spray (random start time, wider), random pitch, time in ms or synced, feedback, mix; xy pad for frequency and pitch.

items.title: reverb
items.what: algorithmic reverb: pre-delay, size, decay (0.2–20 s), damping, width, mix, low / high cut on the input, diffusion, freeze (infinite tail), output (wet level only).

items.title: convolution reverb
items.what: reverb from an impulse response: 6 factory irs (small room, chamber, plate, concert hall, cathedral, ambience) or drop your own audio (truncated to 10 s). mix starts at 30 %; decay shortens and size stretches the ir; reverse; low / high cut; width. drag the pre-delay and decay markers on the ir view.

items.title: limiter
items.what: brickwall limiter: gain (input drive), ceiling, release. it always adds 5 ms of lookahead latency (compensated) and only catches sample peaks, not true peaks.

items.title: utility
items.what: gain (±36 db), balance pan, width (0–200 %) or mid/side balance, invert l / r, mono, bass mono below a frequency, channel stereo / left / right / swap, dc filter, mute, with output meters.

items.title: color effects: saturator, bitcrusher, auto filter
items.what: saturator: 6 curves, drive, bias, tone, oversampling, auto gain (on by default, so more drive doesn't get louder); it always adds a small fixed latency. bitcrusher: bits, rate, jitter, dither. auto filter: 7 filter types with an envelope follower (listens to the sidechain when one is set) and a syncable lfo with stereo phase. erosion: a very short delay wobbled by a sine, noise or wide (per-side) noise; frequency and amount on an xy pad, width of the noise band; tiny fixed latency. pedal: overdrive / distortion / fuzz, gain (level kept steady), bass / mid (500 hz, 1 khz, 2 khz) / treble, sub boost, output, mix; oversampled with a small fixed latency.

items.title: modulation effects: chorus, phaser, flanger, tremolo
items.what: chorus (chorus / ensemble / vibrato), phaser (2–12 stages), flanger (through-zero option), tremolo (or auto-pan). most have sync to tempo; synced lfos lock to the song position while playing. chorus, phaser and flanger start at 50 % mix.

items.title: dynamics: gate, multiband compressor, transient shaper
items.what: gate (or expander, flip, lookahead, sidechain), 3-band multiband compressor with movable crossovers and per-band solo / bypass (the sidechain keys all three bands), transient shaper (attack / sustain boost or cut, clip).

items.title: analysis: spectrum and tuner
items.what: spectrum analyzer (block size, averaging, channel incl. mid / side, range, slope, peak hold) and tuner (reference 415–466 hz, mute output for silent tuning). audio passes through unchanged; they only draw while their window is open.

items.title: midi effects: arpeggiator, chord, scale, note length, velocity, random, pitch
items.what: arpeggiator (9 styles, rate, gate, octaves + distance, swing, hold, retrigger; runs from a free clock when stopped), chord (up to 6 shifted notes, strum), scale (follows track / project scale or custom), note length, velocity (curve / range / random), random (deterministic from seed, so renders repeat), pitch (transpose + block / fold / limit to a range).

items.title: external instrument / external audio effect
items.what: route midi out to hardware and its audio back in (instrument), or send audio out through hardware and back (effect). "measure" times the round trip and sets latency. ports this machine lacks stay selected but are marked missing and the device is silent; on the web the routing is read-only.

areas.name: Racks, drum rack, modulation and sidechain

items.title: group a device into a rack
items.what: right-click a device header > "group into instrument rack / audio effect rack / midi effect rack" wraps that one device in a new rack (not available for drum racks or devices already inside a rack or pad).

items.title: rack chains
items.what: a rack shows one row per chain with mute, solo, volume, pan and delete; expand a row to see its devices. drop a device card on a chain's row to move it there. solo: click = only this chain, ⌘/ctrl-click adds or removes from the soloed set.

items.title: chain zones: keys, velocity, chain select
items.what: each chain's settings button sets which keys, velocities and chain selector values (0–127) it responds to; the rack's chain selector parameter picks chains, so you can switch sounds with one knob or automation.

items.title: rack content rules and nesting depth
items.what: audio effect racks take audio effects, midi effect racks midi effects, instrument racks anything (including a drum rack, unless under a drum pad). racks nest up to 6 levels; the deepest chains offer no racks.

items.title: rack macros
items.what: every rack has 8 macros (0–1). to map one, drag its handle onto a parameter of a device inside the rack, or click it then click the parameter. a macro can drive many parameters, each with its own depth.

items.title: rack presets keep the whole rack
items.what: saving a preset on a rack stores its chains, devices, modulators and mappings; loading it rebuilds them in one undo step.

items.title: drum rack pads
items.what: a drum rack shows 4×4 pads per bank (default bank starts at c1 = note 36; c3 = 60, like ableton). drop a sample on a pad to create it; press and hold to audition through the pad's chain; double-click to rename; each pad has volume, pan, tune and its own device chain.

items.title: choke groups
items.what: give pads the same choke group (1–16) so one cuts the other off, e.g. open and closed hi-hats.

items.title: pad solo isn't saved or undoable
items.what: soloing pads (click = only this pad, ⌘/ctrl-click to add) is live state only: it isn't saved with the project and isn't an undo step.

items.title: slice a sample into a drum rack
items.what: a drum rack window's "slice to pads" (pick a sample, or drop one on the button) cuts a sample at its transients into one pad per slice, above the rack's pads, each with a sampler playing its slice. a browser sample's right-click menu has "slice to new drum rack" (a new MIDI track) and "slice to the selected drum rack"; an audio clip's has "slice to drum rack" (its sample, on a new MIDI track below). each is one undo step.

items.title: adding a modulator
items.what: + modulator (or right-click > add modulator) adds an lfo, envelope, envelope follower, steps, random, keytrack or velocity modulator to a device. only devices directly on a track's chain can host modulators (not devices inside rack chains or drum pads).

items.title: mapping a modulator to parameters
items.what: click a modulator's map button, then click the parameters it should move (shift keeps mapping more, esc stops), or drag its handle onto a parameter. reachable parameters light up. a modulator can reach its own device, or devices inside it when it's on a rack.

items.title: modulation depth chips and rings
items.what: each mapping draws a coloured ring on the knob (base to base + depth) and a live dot while playing; under the control a chip per mapping: drag up/down for depth, double-click for 0, right-click to invert or remove. new mappings start at 50 % depth.

items.title: modulator types
items.what: lfo (shape, rate or sync, phase, retrigger free / note / transport, fade in), envelope (adsr + velocity), envelope follower (attack, release, gain; can listen to another track), steps (1–16 steps, rate, smooth), random (rate or sync, smooth), keytrack (low/high key) and velocity (low/high).

items.title: sidechain a device
items.what: devices with a sidechain input (compressor, limiter, gate, multiband compressor, auto filter, sidechain-capable plugins) show a sidechain selector in their header: pick a source track, then its tap point: pre fx, post fx or post mixer of the track or of one of its rack chains / drum pads. choices that would create a loop are disabled.

items.title: sidechain from your own track or a muted track
items.what: a device can key from its own track's pre fx signal or an earlier rack chain; muting or soloing the source track doesn't silence the sidechain feed.

items.title: show automation lanes
items.what: click the automation icon in a track header to open its lanes (first time: its automated lanes, or volume; master shows tempo first). "+ parameter…" adds another lane; the picker's "active" filter lists only automated parameters. or right-click a device knob > show automation lane.

items.title: adding points
items.what: double-click empty lane space to add a point; it's placed on the second press, so you can keep holding and drag to position it before releasing. a lane is created by its first point. there's no freehand pencil mode.

items.title: editing points
items.what: click / shift-click / ⌘-click to select, add or toggle points; ⌘-drag empty space for a marquee; drag to move (snaps to grid, alt = off grid, ⌘ = lock axis); double-click a point deletes it; arrow keys nudge (shift = bigger value step, smaller time step); backspace deletes; ⌘a selects all.

items.title: shift snaps values to round numbers
items.what: while dragging a point, shift moves continuous values in whole increments (1 db, 1 %, 1 st, 0.01 pan…); stepped parameters (semitones, choices, toggles) always snap.

items.title: curves
items.what: alt-drag a segment to bend it; the lane header's curve menu sets linear / step / smooth for the segments after selected points; right-click a point offers the same.

items.title: set an exact value
items.what: right-click a point > set value… opens a small field: type a value in the parameter's unit, enter applies, esc cancels.

items.title: time ranges in a lane
items.what: drag empty lane space to select a time range in that lane; ⌘c / ⌘x / ⌘v / ⌘d / backspace then copy, cut, paste, duplicate or delete the automation in the range while keeping the curve outside it. pasting into another parameter remaps values.

items.title: lane height and value zoom
items.what: drag a lane's bottom edge to resize (8 px steps, alt = free, double-click resets); on the value scale: scroll/drag to move, ⌘/ctrl-scroll to zoom, double-click to reset. stepped parameters open zoomed so steps are visible (e.g. ±3 st for transpose).

items.title: moving an automated knob doesn't stick
items.what: an automated parameter follows its lane during playback and when stopped; turning the knob changes it only until the engine resends the automated value. there is no automation recording and no ableton-style override / re-enable button: turn the lane off with its ⏻ button to use the knob.

items.title: hide vs disable vs delete a lane
items.what: × hides the lane (points kept), ⏻ disables it (kept, ignored by playback), ⌫ in the lane header deletes the lane and all its points.

items.title: device on/off automation
items.what: the device on switch can be automated; while it is, the power button's tooltip says the device is on/bypassed by automation and a click only changes it where it isn't automated.

items.title: clip envelopes
items.what: clips can have their own envelopes (piano roll lane picker, or the warp editor's strip for audio clips). they move and loop with the clip, and while the clip plays they override the track's lane for that parameter. audio clips add clip gain and transposition envelopes, which add to the clip's value instead.

items.title: automation vs modulation
items.what: automation writes absolute values on the timeline (one lane per parameter); modulation (modulators, macros) moves a parameter around its current value continuously, with a depth. both can apply to the same parameter.

items.title: automation on touch
items.what: on phones, lanes are shown from the track sheet and points are added, moved and deleted by touch.

items.title: plugins are desktop only
items.what: the desktop app hosts clap, vst3 and au (macos only). the web app has no plugins: its device library lists factory devices only, and plugin folder settings aren't available.

items.title: plugin folders and scanning
items.what: settings > plugins: system folders on/off (default on, also covers au), add your own folders (each limited to one format or any). rescan only loads new or changed plugins; full rescan reloads everything and retries failures. scans run in separate processes in parallel, so a bad plugin can't crash the app.

items.title: failed plugins and retry
items.what: settings > plugins > failed plugins lists plugins that couldn't load with the reason; right-click > retry… scans one again with a longer timeout (up to 60 min, for huge libraries or shell plugins).

items.title: same plugin in several formats
items.what: a plugin installed as clap and vst3 appears once per format with a format chip; use the format toggles in the library to hide formats you don't use.

items.title: plugin editor windows
items.what: the window button in a plugin's header opens its own editor in a separate native window that stays above the main window. the generic parameter list on the card shows the plugin's own value text.

items.title: linux: plugin editors need x11
items.what: on linux, plugin editors need an x display (xwayland on wayland).

items.title: keys in plugin windows
items.what: while a plugin window has focus, space still controls ethereal's transport (and the play shortcuts); when computer-keyboard midi is on, its note keys play ethereal instead of going to the plugin. ctrl / alt / cmd combinations always reach the plugin.

items.title: sandboxing and crashes
items.what: by default plugins run inside the app. right-click a plugin header > "run sandboxed (crash-safe, +1 block latency)" moves it into its own process; if it crashes the device shows crashed · bypassed with reload, and the app keeps running.

items.title: open without plugins (safe mode)
items.what: the project list's row menu and the crash recovery dialog offer "open without plugins": plugin devices stay bypassed placeholders (state kept) until you click load on one or "load plugins" in the top bar.

items.title: missing plugins
items.what: a project using a plugin that isn't installed keeps the device (and its saved state) as missing · bypassed, so the track plays dry. install it, rescan, and the header says found · reload; reload restores it with its state. right-click > resolve… or replace plugin… swaps it for another plugin, optionally keeping automation and parameters.

items.title: plugin state is saved in the project
items.what: each plugin's full state is stored in the project file (by format and plugin id, not path), so it opens on any machine with the plugin installed; quitting saves live plugin states.

items.title: plugin presets
items.what: the device preset menu also saves and loads plugin presets (the plugin's full state), stored per plugin in the user library; loading is one undo step.

items.title: the browser
items.what: the left rail's browser lists your library by kind: samples, midi, presets, projects. without a search it shows the library folders as a tree; typing searches the whole indexed library (matching folders first). sort by name, recent, duration, bpm or relevance; star favourites; tags.

items.title: preview samples
items.what: click a sample (or use ↑ ↓ from the search field) to preview it; click again to stop. "sync" previews in time with the project tempo and is remembered. esc clears the search.

items.title: drag samples into the project
items.what: drag a sample onto a track to make an audio clip there, or onto empty space below the tracks to create a new audio track with it (one undo step); also onto a sampler, a drum pad, a multisampler key or a convolution reverb's ir view.

items.title: midi files from the browser
items.what: midi files are listed under the midi chip; dropping one on a midi track or below the tracks turns it into midi clips (one per file track, #717). clips and tracks can be exported as midi files.

items.title: presets in the browser
items.what: the presets view lists factory and user presets; enter, a click or right-click > load on… loads one onto a matching factory device on the selected track. if there's none you get "select a track with a … device". presets can't be dragged onto tracks.

items.title: add your own folders
items.what: desktop: "add folder…" indexes a folder in place (files aren't copied). web: "import folder…" copies the folder's audio into the library. dropping a folder from your computer on the browser does the same. right-click a folder: rescan, rename, remove folder.

items.title: folder depth limit
items.what: sub-folders are walked up to 16 levels deep; hidden files and folders (.ds_store, .git) are skipped.

items.title: tags and favourites
items.what: right-click an item: favourite, edit tags… (comma-separated), show in folder, filter by a tag; tag chips on rows filter the list.

items.title: packs
items.what: sample packs show inside their library root as their own folder (a pack's name is kept as written).

items.title: file filter rules
items.what: settings > general > library: "show" and "hide" regex rules on file names decide which files the browser lists (hide wins; empty show = all). invalid rules are marked inline and the status says how many files they'd show; reset to defaults restores supported types.

items.title: project media and open projects
items.what: the browser can also show the current project's media; the projects view opens a project on enter or right-click > open project.

areas.name: Import from other DAWs and audio import

items.title: resolve missing devices / samples
items.what: closing the report (done) opens "resolve missing items": each missing plugin, device kind and audio file with a proposed replacement, its confidence (same plugin id, same name, same family, similar name) and why. switch items on, pick another, or leave them; apply is one undo step.

items.title: resolve later, and getting back to it
items.what: every item can be left for later. the list stays reachable from the top bar's "n missing" badge, the project menu, a missing device's "resolve…" button, right-click "resolve…" on a missing clip or device, and the palette ("resolve missing devices and samples…").

items.title: "show when a project opens" switch
items.what: the resolver pops up whenever you open a project with missing items. the "show when a project opens" toggle in the dialog turns that off (per user).

items.title: replacing a missing device carries values over
items.what: replacing a missing device (by a built-in of the same role or any installed plugin) moves values, automation, modulation and midi mappings to parameters with the same name ("drywet" = "dry/wet" = "mix"); what has no match is listed in a notification.

items.title: plugin state kept only for the same plugin
items.what: a missing plugin replaced by another version or format of the same plugin keeps its saved sound; replaced by a different plugin, only parameter values mapped by name (or index) survive and the dialog lists what is lost.
