items.title: ai suggestions for missing plugins (optional)
items.what: if an ai provider is set up in the ai chat, unsure plugin matches can be sent to it. only plugin metadata is sent, you see the payload ("show what will be sent") and consent once; suggestions are marked "ai suggestion" and only apply when you switch them on.

items.title: finding missing audio files
items.what: missing audio is matched by file name, then sample rate, channels and length (and content hash when known), in the imported project's folder, its parents' samples/ folders, the library, and a folder you choose (desktop).

items.title: import audio files (⌘i / ctrl+i)
items.what: "import audio…" (⌘i / ctrl+i, the palette, the arrangement and browser menus) adds wav, aiff, flac, mp3, ogg, m4a/aac files: on the selected audio track at the selection cursor (not the playhead), one after another, else each on a new audio track. the whole import is one undo step.

items.title: dropping audio vs project files
items.what: drop audio on the arrangement lanes to place it where you drop, or on the browser to only add it to the project. dropping a .als/.flp/.rpp/.dawproject anywhere imports it as a new project instead; a dropped .ether project opens as a new project too.

items.title: audio import limits and errors
items.what: files over 1 gb, empty files and unsupported types are refused before upload ("use wav, aiff, flac, mp3 or ogg"); a failed file stays in the import list until dismissed and doesn't stop the others; once uploaded, an import can no longer be cancelled.

areas.name: Export audio and export to other DAWs

items.title: export audio dialog
items.what: project menu > export audio… opens a dialog: range, format, bit depth, sample rate, tail, file name, normalize and stems. defaults: whole project, wav, 24-bit, engine rate, no tail.

items.title: where exported files go
items.what: the desktop app writes into the project's exports/ folder ("saved in the project folder"), never overwriting: a taken name gets " (2)". the browser downloads each file, with "download again" buttons until you close the dialog.

items.title: range options and the "selected clips" range
items.what: range is whole project (up to the end of the last clip or track automation point), loop region, or "selected clips": the time selection (shift-drag) when there is one, else the span of the selected clips. it's disabled until something is selected.

items.title: tail for reverb and delay
items.what: tail adds 0 to 60 seconds after the range end so reverbs and delays ring out. it defaults to 0.

items.title: formats, bit depth and sample rate rules
items.what: wav (16-bit dithered, 24-bit, 32-bit float), flac (16 or 24-bit only) or mp3 at 320 kbps (no bit depth, 44.1 or 48 khz only). sample rate is the engine rate, 44.1, 48, 88.2 or 96 khz; incompatible choices are greyed out.

items.title: normalize
items.what: normalize scales each file so its peak sits at -0.1 dbfs (each stem on its own). it is peak normalization, not loudness.

items.title: stems: what each file contains
items.what: with stems on, each chosen track is exported alone: its chain, fader and pan into the master, plus what it sends to returns. solo is ignored, a muted track is unmuted for its own stem, a track in a group skips the group's processing, and the master's devices are left out. audio and midi tracks are chosen by default.

items.title: overlapping stems
items.what: choosing a track together with its group, or with a return it sends to, puts that audio in both files; sidechain sources from other tracks are silent in a stem.

items.title: export keeps running when the dialog is closed
items.what: closing the dialog during a render keeps it going; the top bar shows "export n%" and a click reopens it. cancel export stops it.

items.title: large exports in the browser
items.what: in the browser, files stay in memory until downloaded; above about 200 mb the dialog warns. normalize also holds the whole render in memory on every platform.

items.title: a plugin that can't render offline fails the export
items.what: export renders offline with fresh plugin instances; a plugin that can't be created that way stops the export with an error instead of being skipped.

areas.name: Keyboard shortcuts and the command palette

items.title: command palette (⌘k / ctrl+k)
items.what: ⌘k / ctrl+k (or the rail's last button) opens a searchable list of commands: type part of a name, ↑/↓ to move, enter to run, escape to close. recently run commands come first; shortcuts shown follow your keymap.

items.title: commands only in the palette
items.what: print keyboard shortcuts, mouse and wheel settings…, duplicate project, rename project, zoom to fit, go to track <name>, pin/unpin browser/inspector/editor drawer, relink missing samples…, turn midi mode on/off, and debug panels have no menu entry elsewhere.

items.title: transport shortcuts
items.what: space: play / stop and go back to where play started. shift+space: play / stop in place. record, loop and metronome have no default key (the ableton-like preset adds f9 for record and ⌘l / ctrl+l for loop).

items.title: edit shortcuts
items.what: ⌘z undo, ⇧⌘z or ctrl+y redo, ⌘c copy, ⌘x cut, ⌘v paste at the selection cursor, ⌘d duplicate, ⌘a select all, backspace/delete delete (also with shift or alt), escape deselect / close the piano roll, ⌘e split at the cursor or time selection. (ctrl instead of ⌘ on windows/linux.)

items.title: copy / cut / paste act on the time selection when there is one
items.what: with a time selection (shift-drag), ⌘c, ⌘x, ⌘d and backspace act on that time range rather than clips; ⌘v pastes a time copy right after the selection so repeated pastes tile it; ⌘e splits the range.

items.title: time selection shortcuts
items.what: in the arrangement: ⇧⌘x cut time, ⇧⌘c copy time, ⇧⌘v paste time (insert, shifting later material), ⇧⌘d duplicate time, ⇧⌘i insert silence, ⇧⌘backspace / ⇧⌘delete delete time.

items.title: arrangement shortcuts
items.what: ⇧⌘l clip loop on/off, r reverse clip (or selected notes), ⌘g group selected tracks, ⇧⌘g ungroup, ↑ / ↓ previous / next take in a comp region. add audio / midi track have no default key (ableton-like: ⌘t, ⇧⌘t).

items.title: piano roll shortcuts
items.what: ⌘u quantize, b draw mode, ↑/↓/←/→ (or with alt) nudge notes, shift+↑/↓ octave up/down, shift+←/→ also nudge, r reverse selected notes.

items.title: automation lane shortcuts
items.what: arrows (or alt+arrows) nudge selected points; shift+↑/↓ moves the value one increment (1 db, 1 %…), shift+←/→ a fine time step.

items.title: app and view shortcuts
items.what: ⌘s save, ⌥⌘s save snapshot…, ⌘i import audio…, ⌘j show / hide the editor drawer (ableton-like adds ⌥⌘l), ⇧⌘a ask ai, ⇧⌘m focus the collab chat (in a session). open the browser and zoom to fit have no default key (ableton-like: ⌥⌘b for the browser).

items.title: computer midi keyboard (m)
items.what: m turns the computer keyboard into a piano: a w s e d f t g y h u j k o l p ; play notes, z / x octave down / up, c / v velocity down / up. while it's on, those letters stop triggering other shortcuts (r, b…); keys with ⌘/ctrl/alt and space still work.

items.title: mouse modifiers
items.what: alt+drag a clip without snapping, ⌘/ctrl+drag copies clips, ⌘⇧/ctrl+shift+drag slips a clip's content. these are fixed (not in the keymap).

items.title: customizing shortcuts
items.what: palette > keyboard shortcuts… (or settings > input > edit keyboard shortcuts…, #717) lists every action by group with search (by name or key). + records a new chord (enter confirms, escape cancels), × removes one, the arrow resets a row; up to 4 chords per action. "reset all to ethereal defaults" undoes everything.

items.title: ableton-like preset
items.what: the keymap editor's preset switch adds ableton live's chords (f9 record, ⌘l loop, ⌘t / ⇧⌘t new audio / midi track, ⌥⌘b browser, ⌥⌘l editor) on top of the defaults; nothing is removed.

items.title: conflicts
items.what: two actions on the same key where both apply are flagged on both rows; "conflicts only" filters to them. when recording a taken chord you can "use anyway" or unbind the other action.

items.title: any palette command can get a shortcut
items.what: every palette command (add a device, open a panel, share…) is listed in the keymap editor and can be bound, except per-project entries like "go to track".

items.title: print the cheat sheet
items.what: palette > print keyboard shortcuts prints every current shortcut, plus the mouse modifiers.

items.title: where shortcuts are saved
items.what: the keymap is saved in your user library and follows other windows. if the engine can't store it, the editor says "changes last until you close ethereal".

items.title: ctrl vs ⌘ on mac
items.what: on macos shortcuts use ⌘; a ctrl chord that nothing binds falls back to the ⌘ action. on windows and linux ctrl and ⌘ are the same key in the keymap.

items.title: browser shortcuts that win on the web
items.what: in a browser tab, keys the browser reserves (⌘t / ctrl+t new tab, ⇧⌘t reopen tab, ⌘w, ⌘n) never reach ethereal, so the ableton-like ⌘t / ⇧⌘t can't add tracks there. other bound keys (⌘s, ⌘d, ⌘j, ⌘k) are taken over by the app inside the page.

items.title: shortcuts in text fields and plugin windows
items.what: shortcuts are ignored while typing in a text field. native plugin windows forward space and, with the computer midi keyboard on, its keys, so you can play from inside a plugin.

items.title: phones show a 'not available' screen
items.what: in a phone's browser, ethereal shows "ethereal is not available on mobile — try it on desktop" with "copy link" and "try the mobile beta". touch-only tablets are blocked too; an ipad with a keyboard or trackpad gets the desktop app.

items.title: turning on the mobile beta
items.what: "try the mobile beta" or adding ?mobile=1 to the url boots the touch interface; it's remembered for the tab, ?mobile=0 turns it off, ?force-desktop forces the desktop editor.

items.title: the mobile layout
items.what: top bar with the project menu, undo / redo, share and settings; the arrangement; a bottom transport (stop, play/pause, record, loop, metronome) with position, tempo and a follow-playhead button. in phone landscape the bars move to one bottom row. no side rail, browser or device windows.

items.title: pan, pinch and momentum
items.what: one-finger drag scrolls the timeline (locked to one axis when the move is mostly along it) and keeps gliding when flicked. pinch with fingers side by side zooms time; one above the other changes track height.

items.title: tap, double-tap, long-press
items.what: tap = click, double-tap = double-click (within 300 ms), long-press (about half a second, 450 ms) = right-click menu. android gives a short vibration.

items.title: panning stops following the playhead
items.what: the view follows the playhead by default; panning while playing stops following. the transport's follow-playhead button brings it back.

items.title: empty arrangement: double-tap to make a clip
items.what: on an empty arrangement the hint reads "double-tap a midi track's lane to make a clip"; there is no sample browser to drag from on mobile.

items.title: track headers on touch
items.what: tap a header to select the track, tap the selected one again to open its track sheet, long-press for its menu, long-press then drag to reorder (or drop into a group). on phones the header only shows mute, solo and arm.

items.title: the track sheet
items.what: mute / solo / arm, larger volume and pan, rename, move up / down, cut, copy, paste, duplicate, delete, an "automation" toggle and the device list. devices are read-only ("edit devices on a computer for now").

items.title: sheets close with back
items.what: sheets slide up from the bottom; drag the handle up to make them taller, down to shrink or close; tap outside, press escape or use the system back gesture to close. back closes the sheet instead of leaving the project.

items.title: moving clips: select first or long-press
items.what: a drag on a selected clip moves it (and the rest of the selection); on an unselected clip a plain drag scrolls instead, so long-press first to move it. a badge above your finger shows where it lands (snapped); near the edges the view scrolls; a second finger cancels the drag.

items.title: trim handles only on selected, wide-enough clips
items.what: only a selected clip has trim handles: 44 px touch targets on each edge, half outside the clip. a clip narrower than 24 px on screen has none: zoom in or use the clip sheet's numbers.

items.title: the clip action bar
items.what: selecting clips shows a bar at the bottom: select more, edit, split, duplicate, copy, paste, earlier / later, position, delete and more (the full clip menu).

items.title: select more (multi-select without shift)
items.what: "select more" makes taps add or remove clips and a drag on empty lane space draw a selection box; "done (n)" ends it, and it ends by itself when nothing stays selected.

items.title: nudge by one grid step
items.what: the clip bar's earlier / later (◀ ▶) move the selection by one grid step at the current zoom (a beat when the grid is off), never before the song start.

items.title: time range with handles
items.what: long-press then drag on empty lane space selects a time range (the desktop's shift-drag). two grips, like text selection, drag its ends (snapped; drag one past the other and they swap). its own bar offers copy, cut, paste, duplicate, loop it, delete time and more.

items.title: clip sheet: typed position
items.what: "position" in the clip bar (one clip) opens a sheet to type the start as bar.beat.sixteenth (1-based, "3" = bar 3) and the length as bars.beats.sixteenths (0-based, "0.2" = two beats), and to nudge each edge one grid step. invalid input reverts; each change is one undo step.

items.title: clip editor and piano roll on touch
items.what: double-tap a clip (or "edit") opens its editor over the arrangement; close with the button or back. in the piano roll: select mode taps select, double-tap adds/deletes a note, drag a selected note to move (edge to resize), long-press-drag draws a box; the draw toggle makes taps add notes. on phones the velocity lanes are hidden until "velocity" is tapped.

items.title: automation on touch
items.what: open lanes from the track sheet's "automation". double-tap adds a point, double-tap a point deletes it, long-press then drag moves a point (or selects a range on empty space); a plain drag only scrolls.

items.title: the mixer view and fine mode
items.what: the transport's mixer button switches to channel strips (master pinned right). faders and knobs move relative to where you grab them; slide your finger sideways while dragging for fine control; double-tap resets.

items.title: leaving the app stops playback
items.what: when the page is hidden (another app, lock screen, a call), playback stops and a recording take is finished; coming back does not resume.

items.title: rotating keeps your place
items.what: turning the device keeps the beat at the centre of the screen in the centre, and switches between the portrait and landscape layouts.

items.title: what's missing on mobile
items.what: no command palette, keyboard shortcuts, sample browser, device editing or plugin windows, midi mapping, guided tours or ai chat. the project menu's "export audio…" has no dialog in the mobile shell, so audio export needs a computer for now. "report an issue…" is in the project menu.

items.title: projects, sharing and settings on a phone
items.what: dialogs open full screen, controls are 44 px, and on the project screen each row shows rename, duplicate and delete directly (no hover). invite links work on phones with ?mobile=1.

items.title: ask ai panel
items.what: the "ask ai" tab in the left rail (cmd/ctrl+shift+a, or the command palette) lets you ask a model to edit the open project: create tracks, write midi, add devices, set parameters, mix, tempo, transport, export.

items.title: bring your own api key
items.what: the chat needs a provider and model: anthropic (default), openai, deepseek, gemini, mistral, groq, openrouter, together, or local ollama / lm studio (no key). you paste your own key; usage is billed by that provider. "test connection" checks it.

items.title: where your key is stored
items.what: desktop: in ethereal's app data on this computer. web: in this browser's local storage, readable by anyone using that browser profile. it is only sent to the chosen provider.

items.title: what is sent to the ai provider
items.what: your messages plus an overview of the project (track, clip, device and section names, mixer, tempo) and whatever the model reads with its tools (notes, parameters) go to the provider. no audio files. the chat asks for consent once per provider before the first message (#717).

items.title: each ai action is one undo step
items.what: every edit the ai makes is applied immediately as one undo step labelled "ai: <action>"; cmd/ctrl+z undoes it. in a session, ai edits sync to everyone like your own.

items.title: tool calls, stop and round limit
items.what: each tool the ai runs shows as an expandable row (input, result, errors). a reply pauses after 25 tool rounds by default (settings: "tool rounds per message", up to 200); stop aborts the turn.

items.title: switching provider starts fresh
items.what: changing provider mid-conversation starts a new conversation ("it starts fresh and doesn't see the messages above"). the conversation is kept per project on this computer and restored on reload; "clear chat" forgets it (#717).

items.title: web: cors blocks some providers
items.what: in the browser some providers refuse direct requests; the panel detects it and suggests a fix (set OLLAMA_ORIGINS for ollama, enable cors in lm studio, or use openrouter / a proxy). the desktop app isn't affected.

items.title: models without tool support
items.what: some local models can't call tools; the panel says so and suggests another model.

items.title: what the ai can't do
items.what: the ai works only through ethereal's tools: no arbitrary files, no running commands, no opening other projects. plugin search lists nothing on the web; library search needs the sound browser index.

items.title: external ai agents (mcp)
items.what: desktop only: "allow external ai agents (mcp)" in the ai settings lets claude code, claude desktop or other mcp clients on this computer edit the open project live. it shows the port, connected clients and a copyable "claude mcp add" command. off by default; loopback only with a fresh token each time.

items.title: ether-mcp isn't bundled yet
items.what: the copied command runs ether-mcp, but the binary isn't shipped with the app: it has to be built from source (cargo build -p ether-mcp). if the app is closed or the toggle off, calls fail with "ethereal is not reachable…" and work again once enabled, without restarting the client.
items.removed: #662 ships ether-mcp with the desktop app; advanced/mcp#connecting-claude-code documents the current setup

items.title: mcp headless and remote modes
items.what: ether-mcp --project song.ether edits a project file with no app and no sound; --server ws://host:port --token t drives an ether-server.

areas.name: Remote engine and web vs desktop

items.title: engine server (remote engine)
items.what: settings > advanced > engine server connects this window to an ether-server on another machine (address ws://host:port plus token) instead of the built-in engine. the top bar shows "● <server>" while connected; disconnect returns to the local engine. the section is hidden until turned on (palette "engine server…", ?engine-server on the web, or an address used before), since ether-server isn't in a release (#717).

items.title: what runs where with an engine server
items.what: the project, plugins and audio processing live on the server and play through the server's audio device, not your computer's speakers. several windows can connect to one server and see each other's edits.

items.title: engine server security
items.what: ether-server listens on 127.0.0.1 by default; exposing it (--listen) requires a token, and anything beyond a trusted network should go through tls. connection errors: wrong token, incompatible version, server busy.

items.title: uploading audio to an engine server
items.what: dropping audio files on the sample browser while connected uploads them to the server and imports them; progress shows in the top bar. unfinished uploads are lost if you disconnect.

items.title: web vs desktop: plugins
items.what: the web version runs the built-in engine in the browser with built-in devices only: vst/clap/au plugins need the desktop app ("plugins are available in the desktop app.").

items.title: web vs desktop: recording and midi
items.what: recording audio/midi and midi learn need the desktop app; the browser picks its audio devices itself.

items.title: web projects live in the browser
items.what: web projects are stored in the browser's private storage (opfs), separate from the desktop app's projects; "open on desktop" doesn't move them. clearing site data deletes them.

items.title: web: phones and big projects
items.what: phones get an "not available on mobile" screen (except static share links, or the mobile beta); the web engine is a ~22 mb download and needs a cross-origin-isolated page. a project too heavy for this engine fails with "graph exceeds engine capacity" (use no engine / another participant's engine in a session).

items.title: web: hosting and dedicated engines
items.what: a web host's live session ends when the tab closes or the computer sleeps, and a browser can't run an engine for others ("the desktop app can").

items.title: remote engine latency
items.what: hearing a participant's engine or a dedicated engine adds a round trip plus encoding delay (tens of ms on a lan, more online). live midi, the on-screen keyboard and recording still go to your own (off) engine and aren't routed to the remote one.

items.title: audio device released with no engine
items.what: on desktop, while your engine is off (no engine, or playing through someone else's), ethereal closes your audio device so other apps can use it; the transport shows "closed".

items.title: Settings overview
items.what: The gear at the top right opens settings with tabs: general (startup, library files, updates), appearance, audio, input (mouse and wheel), plugins, sharing, privacy (telemetry, news) and advanced (sharing servers, remote engine, relay, engine log, debug panels). On the web, audio devices are chosen by the system.

items.title: Command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K)
items.what: Cmd/Ctrl+K, or the last button on the left rail, opens a search over every command: project, transport, panels, templates, help. Commands you ran recently come first. It doesn't open while you're typing in a text field.

items.title: Floating panels: pin, click away, collapse
items.what: The browser (left), inspector (right) and editor drawer (bottom) float over the arrangement. Unpinned, the browser closes when you click in the arrangement and the drawer closes when you click outside it. The pin button keeps a panel open beside the arrangement. The inspector's × shrinks it to a bar, and it opens with the selection.

items.title: Show / hide the editor drawer (Cmd/Ctrl+J)
items.what: Cmd/Ctrl+J toggles the editor drawer (piano roll, warp, automation). With the ableton key preset it's Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+L. Clicking a clip opens its editor in the drawer.

items.title: Undo and redo
items.what: Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Ctrl+Y) redoes. Every edit to the song is undoable, including loop region, tempo, mute and solo. Record-arm, play, stop and locate, opening plugin windows, audio settings and project actions (open, delete, duplicate) are not.

items.title: History panel: jump to any step
items.what: The left rail's "history" tab lists your edits by name. Click one to undo or redo to that point, or right-click for "undo to here" or "redo to here". The first row, "project opened", undoes everything since you opened the project.

items.title: Checkpoints in the undo history
items.what: The flag on a history step, or "name checkpoint…" in the command palette, gives the current step a name so it's easy to find and jump back to.

items.title: Undo history isn't saved
items.what: Undo history and checkpoints are cleared when you reload, switch project or quit. The panel says "not saved with the project". Only the newest 500 steps are kept, and older ones show "older steps were dropped from the history".

items.title: Toasts: which ones stay
items.what: Info messages at the bottom disappear after 6 s, and pause while you hover them. Warnings and errors stay until you close them. Only the 3 newest are shown, and there's no list of past messages.

items.title: "Engine not responding" warning
items.what: If the engine stalls, often because a plugin is busy, a warning says "the engine is not responding: <reason>. Audio keeps playing; your actions will run when it recovers." Afterwards an info message says how long it lasted.

items.title: Engine log (desktop)
items.what: Settings › advanced › "open engine log" opens a terminal that follows the engine's log. It shows warnings, plugin problems and why the engine stalled.

items.title: Debug panels (advanced)
items.what: Settings › advanced lists debug panels, also in the palette as "debug: …". They are floating windows that look inside a feature, and their position and open state are remembered. None are registered at the moment.
